<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT -->
# Squatch Tuner: measured results

Measured on 2026-09-23 on an Apple M1 Max (clang 21, `-O3`, no fast-math) with the code in this
commit. `make results` in the tuner's directory reproduces every number. The raw output is in `results/`. Evidence tags:
**(M)** measured here, **(E)** estimate.

## Setup

- **Methods compared.** Four methods share one front end: decimation to 12 kHz, a 64-sample
  (5.3 ms) hop, and the same −70 dBFS gate.
  - **YIN** and **MPM**, each with a median-of-5 smoother, as most tuners use. They also run
    at the full 48 kHz as a stronger baseline.
  - **MPM + phase vocoder:** MPM finds the note. Each partial's phase advance between two
    Hann-windowed frames one period apart gives its frequency, and the same stiffness fit
    as ours combines them.
  - **Squatch strobe:** this repository. `hz` follows the string; `steadyHz` is the window
    average.
- **Synthetic truth.** Plucked, stiff strings from E1 to E6:
  - 12 notes × 8 trials, each detuned at random by up to ±50 c;
  - stiffness B from 3×10⁻⁵ to 3×10⁻⁴;
  - pluck and pickup combs, decay, pick noise;
  - a tension-modulation glide of +g·envelope², so the pluck starts sharp.
  - Accuracy is scored against the true pitch at each moment (glide included). Lock time is
    scored against the settled pitch: the first reading within tolerance after which no
    reading leaves it.
- **Real DI.**
  - Source: the Guitar-TECHS single-note recordings, both players (P1, P2). Pedroza, Abreu,
    Corey and Roman, ICASSP 2025, doi:10.1109/ICASSP49660.2025.10887996, data at
    [Zenodo record 14963133](https://zenodo.org/records/14963133), **CC BY 4.0**.
  - Nothing from the dataset is copied into this repository. The bench reads the files from a
    local copy (`GUITAR_TECHS` in the Makefile).
  - The data: 275 notes that ring at least 1.5 s. Every method runs continuously over each
    whole 9-minute file.
  - No other audio is used: everything else is synthesised by the bench.
  - Real notes have no ground truth, so each file is also resampled up by exactly 7.0 cents
    (band-limited) and each method's measured shift is compared with 7.0.

## Synthetic plucks (M)

RMS error in cents over 0.5–1.5 s after the pluck (0.25–0.5 s for the dead note), against the
true pitch at that moment. Percentages are readings more than 50 c out (octave slips, hum).

| Scenario | YIN | MPM | YIN @48k | MPM @48k | MPM + PV | Squatch `hz` | Squatch `steadyHz` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Clean (60 dB SNR) | 2.75 | 1.23 | 0.128 | 0.032 | 0.029 | **0.001** | 0.001 |
| Guitar pluck | 3.97 | 1.90 | 1.31 | 1.23 | 0.036 | **0.036** | 0.220 |
| Fundamental −20 dB | 316 (8.2%) | 204 (1.5%) | 315 (8.1%) | 65 (0.5%) | 204 (1.5%) | **0.037 (0%)** | 0.216 |
| 30 dB SNR + hum | 190 (5.0%) | 176 (5.1%) | 117 (5.7%) | 56 (1.3%) | 177 (4.9%) | **0.055 (0%)** | 0.231 |
| Hard pluck (15 c glide) | 3.90 | 2.21 | 1.47 | 1.38 | **0.171** | 0.178 | 1.08 |
| Dead note (T60 0.6 s) | 3.17 | 1.39 | 3.05 | 1.08 | 0.165 | 0.021 | **0.020** |

Lock times (median / p90, ms):

| | YIN | MPM | MPM @48k | MPM + PV | Squatch `hz` | Squatch `steadyHz` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ±1 c, clean | 55 / 65 | 44 / 65 | 39 / 65 | 44 / 108 | **39 / 87** | 39 / 92 |
| ±0.1 c, clean | 1484 / 1500 | 471 / 1487 | 65 / 1479 | 1457 / 1500 | **44 / 145** | 44 / 148 |
| ±1 c, guitar pluck | 873 / 1283 | 839 / 1306 | 892 / 1341 | 500 / 657 | **465 / 604** | 639 / 839 |
| ±1 c, dead note | 204 / 455 | 151 / 435 | 156 / 441 | 97 / 439 | **87 / 103** | 92 / 108 |

On the guitar pluck, ±1 c of the settled pitch takes about half a second whatever the method,
because the string is still gliding. Ablations, also in `results/synth.md`:

- **Without the stiffness fit**, the guitar-pluck error rises to 1.29 c. That is the
  stiff-string bias.
- **With only the line fit** (`steadyHz`), the error is the window lag during a glide.

Per-note tables are in `results/synth.md`.

## Real guitar DI (M)

| Method | Re-pitch error, median / abs p50 / abs p95 (c) | Jitter p50 (c) | Stable ±1 c p50 / p90 (ms) | Stable ±0.1 c p50 (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| YIN | 0.027 / 0.130 / 0.505 | 0.40 | 776 / 1462 | 1493 |
| MPM | 0.003 / 0.041 / 0.250 | 0.37 | 704 / 1141 | 1483 |
| MPM + PV | −0.001 / 0.058 / 0.293 | 0.53 | 1216 / 1493 | 1493 |
| Squatch `hz` | 0.000 / 0.008 / 0.176 | 0.51 | 864 / 1262 | 1435 |
| **Squatch `steadyHz`** | 0.001 / **0.005 / 0.131** | 0.38 | 715 / 1182 | **1168** |

Notes on this table:

- **Jitter** is the spread 0.5–1.0 s after the pluck. The guitar's own pitch still wanders
  there, so no method can reach zero. **Stable** means the reading stays within the band
  around the note's own settled value (median over 1.0–1.5 s).
- **Coverage.** 270 notes had a Squatch reading in the settled window, against 272 for the
  others.
- **One note is an octave dispute.** A fretted G4 had the open G string ringing in sympathy,
  in tune. Squatch reads G3 and the others G4; the cents agree within 1.3 c. Which side the
  "slip" is counted on depends on which methods form the majority (`results/real.md` against
  `results/real-variants.md`).
- **Stiffness on real strings.** On real strings MPM reads 2 to 6 c sharp of the partial-1
  frequency the strobe measures. Measured partials of a fretted low-E note gave B ≈ 1×10⁻³.

### The pluck glide on real strings (M)

Pitch after the pluck, relative to the settled pitch (1.0–1.5 s), from the Squatch `hz` trace:

| after | 50 ms | 100 ms | 200 ms | 300 ms | 500 ms | 750 ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| p10 | −0.76 | −2.82 | −3.62 | −3.21 | −2.36 | −1.77 |
| median | **+5.22** | +2.06 | +0.85 | +0.22 | −0.06 | −0.17 |
| p90 | +15.0 | +7.85 | +5.25 | +4.16 | +2.23 | +1.59 |

### Variants on the same notes (M, `results/real-variants.md`)

| `steadyHz` variant | abs p50 / p95 (c) | Jitter (c) | Stable ±1 c p50 (ms) | Stable ±0.1 c p50 (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| default (6 partials, 0.5 s) | 0.005 / 0.131 | 0.38 | 715 | 1168 |
| memory 0.35 s | 0.005 / 0.149 | 0.44 | 736 | 1264 |
| memory 0.7 s | 0.004 / 0.187 | 0.38 | 619 | 1128 |
| 3 partials | 0.004 / 0.105 | **0.32** | **579** | 1168 |
| no stiffness fit | 0.004 / 0.107 | 0.48 | 763 | 1301 |

Three partials look better on real notes. That is a candidate default, to be re-checked on the
synthetic suite, where fewer partials weaken the stiffness fit.

## Polyphonic strum check (M, `results/poly.md`)

RMS cents over 300 strums. "Real" is the poly reading minus the mono tuner's reading of the
same open-string pluck alone. The strums mix open strings from P1 with 0–40 ms spread and 0 to
−6 dB levels. "Synthetic" is the error against the true pitch, with every string detuned by
up to ±20 c.

| String | Real 0.5 s | Real 1 s | Synthetic 0.5 s | Synthetic 1 s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E2 | 0.73 | 1.86 | 0.86 | 0.58 |
| A2 | 0.77 | 0.98 | 0.99 | 0.70 |
| D3 | 0.37 | 0.32 | 1.08 | 0.78 |
| G3 | 1.05 | 1.12 | 0.74 | 0.46 |
| B3 | 5.90 | 2.84 | 6.40 | 6.72 |
| E4 | 6.04 | 4.83 | 8.40 | 6.89 |

B3 and E4 fail by frequency separation alone. Every partial of B3 is within 0.3 Hz of a
multiple of E2's 3rd, and E2's 4th, A2's 3rd and E4 coincide. The fix is joint estimation:
subtract the low strings' already-measured partials.

## CPU and memory (`results/perf.md`)

| | ns per 48 kHz sample, playing | Share of one M1 Max core | Quiet |
|---|---|---|---|
| Squatch Tuner (6 partials) | 158.9 | 0.76% | 0.03% |
| Squatch Tuner (3 partials) | 153.4 | 0.74% | 0.03% |
| MPM alone | 438.6 | 2.11% | 0.03% |
| YIN alone | 250.6 | 1.20% | 0.04% |
| MPM + phase vocoder | 490.5 | 2.35% | 0.04% |
| Poly strum check | 27.1 | 0.13% | 0.13% |

All of these are measured (M). Memory is all static (M): `Tuner` 128 kB, `PolyTuner` 234 kB.
Both are sized for the worst case (512-point fit windows, 8 partials, 8 strings). Trimming
them to what is used would bring the mono tuner to about 70 kB (E).

Most of the mono cost is the MPM coarse check. One check is 152k multiply-adds (a 636-sample
window × 318 lags), run every 4th hop while a note rings and every hop at a note's start. On
the pedals (E):

| | While a note rings | At a note's start, or loud unpitched input |
|---|---|---|
| **Daisy (Cortex-M7 480 MHz)** | about 16 M cycles/s = **3%** | about 48 M cycles/s = 10% |
| **ESP32-S3 (240 MHz), plain C** | about 60 M cycles/s = **25%** of one core | about 70% |
| **ESP32-S3 with ESP-DSP and a float fit** | about 21 M cycles/s = **9%** | about 24% |

How the estimates are built:

- **Daisy:** the M7 is scalar float at about 1.5 cycles per multiply-add, and its FPU does
  doubles in hardware.
- **ESP32-S3, plain C:** 5.2 cycles per tap and software doubles in the fits.
- **ESP32-S3, optimised:** ESP-DSP's dot product at about 1.7 cycles per tap, with the fit
  sums made float.
- **Cutting it further:** restrict the coarse check to lags near the current note while
  tracking.
- **Status:** none of these is measured on target yet.

## Live on the Pi 5 (M, 2026-09-24)

The core ran live on a Pi 5 test bench:

- **Hardware.** Raspberry Pi 5 with a UMC204HD, performance governor.
- **Audio.** jackd at 48 kHz, 64 × 3 frames.
- **Software.** `hosts/jack/tuner_live.cpp`, built with g++ 14 at `-O3`.
- **Signal path.** Test tones from `squatch-tone` left MAIN OUTS L at −20 dBFS, went over the
  bench's cable into Input 2, and arrived at −57.5 dBFS peak.
- **Truth.** The DAC and ADC share one clock, so the tone's frequency is the truth.
- **Scoring.** The steady reading 2 to 6 s after each tone started.

| Tone | Truth (c) | Shown | Steady median (c) | Range (c) | Correct note in the stream |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 110.000000 Hz | 0.000 | A2 | 0.000 | −0.004 … +0.003 | 82–86 ms |
| 110 × 2^(7/1200) = 110.445670 Hz | +7.000 | A2 | +7.000 | +6.997 … +7.004 | 55–64 ms |
| the same, A4 = 442 Hz | −0.851 | A2 | −0.851 | −0.854 … −0.848 | 72 ms |
| 81.814031 Hz (E2 −12.5 c) | −12.500 | E2 | −12.500 | −12.504 … −12.494 | 68–93 ms |
| 196.000000 Hz (G3) | +0.020 | G3 | +0.020 | +0.018 … +0.022 | 43–70 ms |
| 329.684682 Hz (E4 +0.3 c) | +0.300 | E4 | +0.300 | +0.299 … +0.301 | 44–51 ms |

Repeat counts:

- A2 and A2 +7 c were each scored 15 times, including 4 cycles straight after a fresh start.
- The other tones were scored 6 times each.
- The note times are from the runs whose log kept them.

**One unexplained run.** In one run of the +7 c tone (1 of 53 tone runs), the steady reading
held at +6.463 c for the whole 4 s, with one excursion to +13.4 c. That run was right after a
restart.

- A constant −0.54 c is what a stiffness estimate of B ≈ 6×10⁻⁴ does to a single-partial
  input. The fit applies B to f0 but only re-learns it while three or more partials count.
- This is a hypothesis, not a finding: B was not logged then.
- It did not reproduce in the next 41 runs, 28 of them with B logged (all B = 0).
- It did not reproduce in 20 offline trials of the same sequence in white noise.
- B is now in the stream (`"B"`), so a recurrence will show its cause.
- Real strings have several partials, which pin B.

**Latency.**

| Stage | Time | How it was measured |
|---|---|---|
| Steady readings, input jack to a drawn frame | 17–20 ms | The page's own measurement (clock offset from the minimum round trip), a Mac on the same Wi-Fi through a local HTTPS proxy. It includes JACK's 1.33 ms capture latency and the 33 ms publish cadence (16.7 ms on average). It excludes the converter and USB delay and the display's scan-out. |
| A new note, tone onset to the correct note in the Pi's stream | 43–93 ms | The core's own lock time plus the output and input paths |

Adding the two, a new note reaches the screen in about 60 to 115 ms.

**CPU, over 30 s, with a tone playing and one browser attached (% of one Cortex-A76 core at
2.4 GHz).**

| Process | CPU |
|---|---|
| `squatch-tuner-live` | 1.0% |
| jackd | 0.8% |
| `serve.py` | 0.3% |
| **Total** | **about 2.2%**, 0.5% of the Pi |

The audio callback took 1.0% of each 1.33 ms period on average; the worst callback seen was
13% of a period. There were no xruns.

## In the browser (M, 2026-09-24)

The same core compiled to WebAssembly (`hosts/wasm`: Emscripten 6.0.10, `-O3`, 31 kB, no
imports) and run in an AudioWorklet in 128-frame blocks, with the page reading it 30 times a
second. `make wasm-test` reproduces both rows.

- **Module alone** (`hosts/wasm/test/core.test.mjs`, Node 22): exact harmonic test tones
  (partials 1–5) at 48 kHz, scored 2 to 4 s after the start.
- **Whole page** (`hosts/wasm/test/browser.test.mjs`): headless Chrome with the tone as its
  microphone (a 16-bit WAV on Chrome's fake capture device, which delivers 44.1 kHz into a
  48 kHz AudioContext, so the browser's resampler is in the path). The Start button is pressed
  and the number the page shows is read 40 times over 4 s, from 2.5 s after the first reading.

| Tone | Truth (c) | Module alone, steady (c) | Page shows | Page's reading (c) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A2, 110 Hz | 0.000 | 0.0000 … 0.0000 | 0.0, 40 of 40 | 0.000 … 0.000 |
| A2 +7 c | +7.000 | +6.9998 … +7.0000 | +7.0, 40 of 40 | +7.000 … +7.000 |
| E2 −12.5 c | −12.500 | −12.5000 … −12.4998 | −12.5, 40 of 40 | −12.500 … −12.500 |
| E4 +0.3 c | +0.300 | +0.3000 … +0.3000 | +0.3, 40 of 40 | +0.300 … +0.300 |

The in-tune seals matched in every sample: both on for A2, the half-cent seal only for E4
+0.3 c, neither for the others. These are clean electronic tones; a plucked string settles as
described above, in the browser as anywhere.

The page also times one second of audio through a second copy of the module on its main
thread: 1.0 to 1.3% of one M1 Max core in headless Chrome.

## Where it fails

- **B3 and E4 in a strum** (above).
- **Sympathetic strings.** A fretted note with an open string ringing in sympathy at nearly
  the same pitch leaves two sources that no single-note method can separate. On a fretted G3,
  the fundamental and 2nd partial disagreed by 17 c. Harmonic weights are smoothed, so the
  reading no longer flips between them, but it can sit between them.
- **The octave of an ambiguous note** (the G4/G3 case above).
- **Hum.** Strong hum at −30 dB with the note decaying into it: readings are withheld (88%
  coverage in that scenario), not wrong.
- **The first ~40 ms** go to the coarse stage naming the note.
- **Real pluck glide.** It limits every method: ±0.1 c of the settled pitch is not reachable
  in the first ~0.3 s of a hard pluck, however good the estimator.

## Reproduce

```sh
make test                      # unit tests under ASan + UBSan
make results                   # everything above, about 20 minutes
make results GUITAR_TECHS=/path/to/guitar-techs
```

================================================================================
FILE: blocks/tuner/bench/quality/README.md    [Docs: Tuner quality suite]
================================================================================

<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT -->
# Tuner quality suite

Proves a tuner build is accurate and steady **as a player sees it**, with ground truth, on every
platform. The Mac run is the reference; the Pi, the phone and the ESP32-S3 probe replay the same
files and are scored by the same code, and any difference between platforms on the same file is a
bug.

```sh
make tuner-quality-test                        # the suite's own tests, and hold.hpp against hold.js
make tuner-quality TUNER_CORPUS=/path/to/di-corpus  # run, then score (build/tuner-quality/scorecard)
```

Nothing from any dataset is in this repository. `TUNER_CORPUS` names a folder laid out as
`public/egfxset/Clean/<pickup>/<string>-<fret>.wav`,
`public/guitar-techs/P{1,2}_singlenotes/P{1,2}_singlenotes/{audio/directinput,midi}/`,
`owner/di-20260924/*.wav`, `public/guitarset/{annotation,audio_hex-pickup_debleeded}/`,
`public/nsynth/{audio/,examples-guitar.json}` and
`public/idmt-smt-guitar/dataset1/<setup>/{audio,annotation}/`; missing parts are skipped. Without
it, only the synthetic set runs.

**Licences.** Every set but one is CC BY 4.0. **IDMT-SMT-Guitar is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0: internal
testing only.** Nothing derived from it may be shipped, published or committed; `--pack` refuses it
(`internalOnly()` in `idmt_cases.hpp`), and the scorecard marks its rows "internal only". The corpus
folder's `LICENSES.md` has each set's source, version, licence and full attribution; the
scorecard's "Data licences" section lists the sets it used.

## The display path

`display_path.hpp` runs a recording exactly as the apps read the tuner:

- `TunerBlock` in fixed blocks of 16 or 64 frames;
- its `Latest<TunerSnapshot>` polled 30 times a second, after the block that crosses each
  1/30 s of file time;
- `toDisplay()` (`hosts/common/display.hpp`), then the phone's `TunerDisplay` rules. A note stays
  1.5 s after release. While live, the number is the reading's cents to 0.1. After release it is
  the hold's median (`hosts/common/hold.hpp`, checked against `hold.js` by `hold_parity.mjs`),
  or `--.-`. Only fresh snapshots enter the hold.

Every platform writes the same frame rows (`io.hpp`, and `hosts/common/tuner_frames.hpp`):
`t_ms,note,octave,cents,hz,valid,shown_cents`.

## Ground truth

| Set | Cases | Truth |
|---|---|---|
| Synthetic (`synth_cases.hpp`, `../synth.hpp`) | 668 | **Exact.** One factor at a time around a realistic pluck on all six open strings: tuning −49.9…+49.9 c (0.1 c steps within ±2 c), stiffness B 0…2×10⁻³, glide 0…40 c, T60 0.6…8 s, SNR 60…10 dB, level −60…−6 dBFS peak, 50/60 Hz hum with 5 harmonics at −40…−20 dB, five pickup positions and mixes, vibrato and bends. Plus low B, drop D, bass E1, F#1 and frets to 24. |
| EGFxSet clean DI | 690 | **Note** from string and fret; **pitch** from the offline reference. |
| Guitar-TECHS single notes (P1, P2) | 2 takes, 279 notes | **Note** and time from the MIDI shipped with each take (the offset to the audio is measured and applied); **pitch** from the reference. |
| Our DI session | 32 takes | Notes known where the take says what was played (open strings, frets 0–12, harmonics, re-plucks, retunes). Chords and free play are scored for steadiness only. Idle takes count false readings. |
| GuitarSet (`guitarset_cases.hpp`) | 298 string tracks (60 recordings), 8,458 notes | **Note** from the JAMS `note_midi`; **pitch over time** from the string's JAMS `pitch_contour` (pYIN, good to a few cents), truth kind `annotated`. Each hexaphonic (debleeded) channel is one string, at 44.1 kHz. Notes of 0.9 s or more also get the offline reference, for the note error. Reported as a moving set (real playing: bends, vibrato, fast lines), with tracking error by time since the note began, moving against still, and the display's lag. |
| NSynth test split, guitar notes (`nsynth_cases.hpp`) | 652 | **Note** from the MIDI label; **pitch** from the offline reference (samples are not guaranteed in tune). Resampled 16 → 48 kHz with `bench::resample` (windowed sinc, 96 taps, Blackman, cut-off 7.6 kHz). Notes outside E1–E6 are reported apart (tier `outside`). |
| IDMT-SMT-Guitar dataset1 (`idmt_cases.hpp`), **internal only** | 312 | **Note** and onset/offset from each note's XML; **pitch** from the offline reference. Four guitar and pickup setups, frets 0–12. |
| Regression (`regression_cases.hpp`) | 5 | **Exact.** One synthetic recording per failure found on real guitars, each made to fail the way the real one did: a note dying into 56 Hz hum, a stiff string's quiet tail, a fundamental that dies first, a slow pitch glide, six open strings ringing together. `test_quality` checks the property each fix must keep. |

**The offline reference** (`reference.hpp`) is deliberately not the tuner's own method:

1. A Blackman-Harris window over 0.5–1.7 s after the onset.
2. Each partial is the maximum of the window's continuous spectrum: a grid, then golden-section
   search.
3. A partial is kept only with 20 dB of SNR against the median spectrum between partials, and
   only if it is clear of every 50/60 Hz harmonic.
4. A stiff-string fit (B is fitted with 3 or more partials; otherwise B = 1×10⁻⁴ is assumed).

Its own error, measured by `test_quality` on synthetic strings with known f0 (clean, 30 dB SNR,
hum at −30 dB, all six strings): **at most 0.065 c**.

For the display comparison, a contour of causal 0.6 s windows every 100 ms follows the string. It
lags a glide as the tuner's own 0.5 s memory does: within 0.46 c of the truth at the window's
centre on a 10 c glide.

`cases.jsonl` records, for each note, the fit's standard error (`ref_unc_cents`) and half the change
between the two halves of the window (`ref_drift_cents`, the string's own movement). Real strings
drift by cents over a note, so real-data errors are only as good as these.

## Measures and thresholds

Defined in `metrics.py`; the thresholds are in `score.py` (`THRESHOLDS`).

| Measure | Pass if |
|---|---|
| **wobble**: peak-to-peak of the shown number about its own straight line, over every 300 ms from 0.5 s after the onset (p95) | ≤ 0.5 c |
| raw peak-to-peak over 300 ms while the truth is steady (moved < 0.2 c) (p95) | ≤ 0.5 c |
| frame-to-frame change of the shown number (p90) | ≤ 0.2 c |
| direction flips of the shown number per second | ≤ 1 |
| wrong note (octave counted apart) among live frames after 100 ms | ≤ 1% |
| \|error\| against the truth, steady state: median / p95 | ≤ 0.1 c / ≤ 1.0 c |
| coverage of 0.1–2 s | ≥ 90% |
| time to settle within ±1 c (median) | ≤ 1 s |

Scoring rules:

- Synthetic conditions a tuner cannot be asked to read cleanly are reported as **stress** and
  kept out of the verdict: 10–20 dB SNR, −60 dBFS, hum at −20 dB, T60 0.6 s, B 2×10⁻³, a 40 c
  glide.
- Vibrato and bends are reported as **moving**.

## Other platforms

- **Pi:** `tuner_quality --platform pi --frames-only 1` on the Pi scores the Pi's arithmetic on
  every case.
- **Pi's live path:** `squatch-tuner-live --file take.wav | node live_frames.mjs` replays a take
  through the live host's own formatting and the web page's `hold.js` and `formatCents`.
- **Phone and S3 probe:** they play the phone pack and write frame rows. Two commands score and
  compare them:
  - `score.py file --case X.case.json --truth X.truth.csv --frames LOG.csv` scores one log;
  - `score.py diff A.csv B.csv` compares two logs line by line.
- `score.py scorecard --run DIR [--run DIR ...] --out DIR` puts every platform in one scorecard,
  with a frame-by-frame comparison of every pair.

## Breakdowns (`breakdowns.py`: statistics in `stats.py`, tracking in `tracking.py`, rendered by `breakdowns_md.py`)

The scorecard also gives:

- **a verdict per set**: each dataset row's steadiness and accuracy on its own, with the checks
  that failed;
- **breakdowns** per string, fret range, pickup or guitar setup, NSynth instrument, pitch band,
  velocity and quality, and GuitarSet style, player, comp or solo, and note length;
- **the pickup question**: EGFxSet's five positions and IDMT's four setups, paired by string and
  fret. Per measure: Friedman's test, Kendall's W as the effect size, and each position's median
  paired difference from a reference position with a bootstrap 95% interval;
- **tracking over time** on GuitarSet: error against the contour by time since the note began,
  moving (≥ 5 c in 100 ms) against still, the lag that best explains the display on a moving
  string, and how often notes of each length are read at all;
- the worst notes of each new set, with file and time, and the data licences.

================================================================================
FILE: contracts/README.md    [Docs: Control contracts]
================================================================================

<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT -->
# Control contracts

One file per block, `<key>.params.json`, in the `cc.squatch.control/1` profile that squatch-skin
defines (`schema/control.schema.json` there). Each file is the only place the block's parameter
ids, keys, ranges, defaults, tapers, steps, labels, roles, meters and identity are written.
Everything else is generated from it:

| Output | By | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `include/squatch/dsp/contracts/<key>.hpp`: the `Param` enum, the `ParamDesc` table, `BlockInfo` | `tools/build-contracts` | the block (it inherits `contracts::<Block>Contract`) and every C++ host |
| `hosts/clap/generated/<key>.cpp`, `plugins.cmake` | `tools/build-contracts` | the CLAP, VST3 and AUv2 plugins |
| LV2 Turtle, WAM 2.0, OSCQuery, MIDI-CI | squatch-skin's own emitters, run by `tools/build-contracts --formats DIR` | the Pi (PiPedal), the browser rig, networked devices, USB-MIDI |

```sh
tools/build-contracts                        # rewrite the generated files
tools/build-contracts --check                # fail if any is stale (make ci runs this)
tools/build-contracts --formats build/contracts   # also LV2/WAM/OSCQuery/MIDI-CI, via squatch-skin
```

The generator checks everything squatch-skin's `checkDescriptor()` checks (u32 ids never reused,
LV2-symbol keys, units, tapers, at most one bypass), plus what a block needs: a C++ class and
header, a semantic version, a state version, an AU subtype, CLAP features, exactly one bypass and
only value roles (`param`, `bypass`, `meter`, `trigger`; footswitch roles belong to devices, not
blocks).

A `trigger` is a 0..1 toggle whose rising edge starts something in the block (a learn). It is
settable and saved like a parameter, but a host passes it on only as a change it was sent, never
when it restores a state, so loading a preset fires nothing. squatch-skin has no trigger role, so
`--formats` hands it to the skin's emitters as a `param` with `"trigger": true` (the LV2 emitter's
convention).

Contracts that `tools/private-paths` lists stay in the development tree: their plugins go to
`hosts/clap/generated/plugins-private.cmake`, which is never exported, instead of `plugins.cmake`.

## Fields squatch-dsp adds to `product`

`version` (semantic, of the sound and parameters), `stateVersion` (goes up when a saved value
would be read differently), `block` and `header` (the C++ class), `description`, `features`
(CLAP feature strings), `auSubtype` (four characters; the AU manufacturer is `SqSt`), and for
blocks that read a file, `files` (the cabinet's impulse response: a path in the saved state,
never a parameter). squatch-skin ignores fields it does not know.

## Ids, order and keys

- `id` is the stable, never-reused number a host automates (the CLAP param id). Parameters use
  small numbers, meters 100 and up.
- `key` is what presets and states store, so a state reads the same on every target.
- In C++ the enum is dense: the settable parameters (triggers among them) in file order, then the
  bypass, then the meters. `kParamCount` counts the first group; `kCount` all of them.
- What a block learns (a noise profile) is not a parameter: it is the block's learned state
  (Block v2 `saveState()`/`loadState()`), carries its own format version, and a plugin saves it
  beside the parameters. `stateVersion` still covers how the saved parameters are read.

## Conventions settled on 2026-09-25

The C++ blocks and the browser rig's JavaScript (`squatch-rig/web/worklets/dsp/`) disagreed, so a
preset did not carry between them. The rule used: **ranges are the union of both sides**, so every
existing preset from either side is representable without clamping; **sign conventions follow the
more common one** in hosts and hardware; **defaults are the C++ block's** (it carries the tests and
the PiPedal heritage) unless that default was unusable. The golden renders did not change.

### Gate (`gate.params.json`)

| Control | C++ before | JS before | Settled |
|---|---|---|---|
| threshold | -120..0, default -90 | -90..-10, default -58 | **-120..0 dB, default -60** (-90 leaves the gate open on any real DI; -60 is what the Pi rig runs) |
| hysteresis | **-30..0**, default -6: close at threshold **+** hysteresis | 0..20, default 6: close at threshold **-** hysteresis | **0..30 dB, default 6, a positive magnitude: the gate closes below threshold - hysteresis** |
| range | -60..-6, default -60 | -90..0, default -70 | **-90..0 dB, default -60**; the ramp rate treats the range as at least 6 dB, so 0 dB still moves |
| attack | 1..500 ms, default 1 | 0.1..50 ms (log), default 1 | **0.1..500 ms, log taper, default 1** |
| hold | 1..100 ms, default 100 | 0..500 ms, default 40 | **0..500 ms, default 100** |
| release | 10..1000 ms, default 330 | 5..1000 ms (log), default 90 | **5..1000 ms, log taper, default 330** |
| bypass, meters | none | none | bypass (id 7); meters `reduction` (dB) and `open` |

### Limiter (`limiter.params.json`)

| Control | C++ before | JS before | Settled |
|---|---|---|---|
| drive | none | key `gain`, 0..18 dB, default 0 | **key `drive`, 0..18 dB, default 0, smoothed 20 ms**, before the limiter (new in C++) |
| ceiling | -24..0, default -1 | -12..0, default -1 | **-24..0 dBTP, default -1** (true peak) |
| release | 10..1000 ms, default 50 | 10..1000 ms (log), default 120 | **10..1000 ms, log taper, default 50** |
| output | none | none | **-24..0 dB, default 0, smoothed 20 ms**, after the final clamp: it only attenuates, so the output never exceeds the ceiling (new on both sides) |
| bypass, meters | none | `grDb` inside the worklet | bypass (id 5); meter `reduction` (dB, the most in the last buffer) |

### What the JavaScript side must change (squatch-rig, not edited here)

1. **Gate** (`web/worklets/dsp/gate.js`): widen threshold to -120..0 (default -60), hysteresis to
   0..30 (sign already right), range to -90..0 (default -60), attack to 0.1..500, hold to 0..500
   (default 100), release to 5..1000 (default 330). The JS detector still differs from the C++
   one (a 20 ms peak envelope and one-pole gain moves against the C++ instantaneous peak and dB-linear
   ramps), so identical settings will still sound slightly different until the rig runs the WASM
   block.
2. **Limiter** (`web/worklets/dsp/limiter.js`): rename the key `gain` to `drive` (and migrate saved
   `.rig.json` presets), widen ceiling to -24..0, release default 120 -> 50, add `output` (-24..0 dB
   after the ceiling). Its lookahead is 2 ms against the C++ 1.5 ms plus the true-peak
   interpolator, so latency differs (the C++ reports 88 samples at 48 kHz: 72 of lookahead and 16 of interpolator).
3. Generate both maps from these contracts, as `tools/build-bloom-contract.mjs` already does for
   Bloom and Trail OD, so they cannot drift again.

================================================================================
FILE: hosts/clap/README.md    [Docs: Desktop plugins: CLAP, VST3, AUv2]
================================================================================

<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT -->
# Desktop plugins: CLAP, VST3, AUv2

`ClapPlugin<Block>` (`clap_plugin.hpp`) turns any squatch-dsp block into a CLAP plugin;
clap-wrapper turns that into VST3 and AUv2. The plugin's identity, version, parameters, meters and
AU codes all come from the block's control contract (`contracts/`), through
`tools/build-contracts`. No custom GUI yet: hosts show their generic parameter view, meters
included (read-only parameters).

| Plugin | Block | CLAP id | AU | Latency at 48 kHz |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Squatch Limiter | `Limiter` (linked stereo) | `cc.squatch.limiter` | `aufx SqLm SqSt` | 88 samples |
| Squatch Gate | `Gate` (linked stereo) | `cc.squatch.gate` | `aufx SqGt SqSt` | 0 |
| Squatch EQ | `Eq` (dual mono in stereo) | `cc.squatch.eq` | `aufx SqEq SqSt` | 0 |
| Squatch Tuner | `TunerBlock` (hears the mid in stereo) | `cc.squatch.tuner` | `aufx SqTn SqSt` | 0 |
| Squatch Cab | `Cabinet` (dual mono; response path in the state) | `cc.squatch.cabinet` | `aufx SqCb SqSt` | 0 |

Blocks that live only in the development tree add their plugins through
`generated/plugins-private.cmake` and their own test-host cases through `tests/extra_*.cpp`; they
build, install and run the same matrix as the plugins above, and neither file is exported.

## Build, install, check

```sh
tools/fetch-plugin-deps     # the pinned commits in deps.lock -> build/deps, validators -> build/tools
make plugins                # build/plugins/bundles: a .clap, .vst3 and .component per plugin
make plugins-install        # copies them into $HOME/Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/{CLAP,VST3,Components}
make plugins-check          # the whole matrix below; summary in build/reports/plugins-check.md
```

Nothing downloads during a build: CMake reads only `build/deps` (clap 1.2.10, clap-wrapper `next`
at e4fdc820, the VST3 SDK 3.8.0 build 66, AudioUnitSDK 1.1.0; all MIT except the Apache-2.0
AudioUnitSDK). Bump a pin in `deps.lock`, then run `make plugins-check` in full.

## What `make plugins-check` runs

- **The headless test host** (`tests/`, `squatch-clap-host`): every requirement case below on every
  plugin, linked in, and again over the built `.clap` bundles as a host loads them.
- **Sanitizer legs** of the test host: ASan+UBSan (the allocation watch then sees `malloc` too),
  TSan (the main thread reads, saves and loads state while the audio thread processes), and
  RealtimeSanitizer (Homebrew LLVM; every `process()` call runs in a nonblocking scope, also over
  the shipped bundles). Each leg first proves it can fail: `--prove-watch` runs a `process()` that
  allocates and locks, which the watch must count and RTSan must abort on.
- **clap-validator** 0.4.1, the **Steinberg VST3 validator** in extended mode, **pluginval** 1.0.4
  at strictness 10 (VST3 and AU; `PLUGINVAL_STRICTNESS` to change) and **auval -strict**.
  pluginval 1.0.4 has no `--rtcheck`; the RTSan leg covers that ground.

## The adapter's requirements, and the evidence

From real host bugs (research notes, frameworks review 2.1). Case names are in `tests/`.

| # | Requirement | How | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Configurable mono and stereo buses, re-read every buffer | `configurable-audio-ports` and `audio-ports-config`: 1->1, 1->2, 2->2. Each call's channel counts come from its buffers | `portConfigurations`; `blockSizesAndLayouts` sends mono buffers to stereo configurations, the reverse, and no input at all; clap-validator layout tests; auval lists exactly `[2,2] [1,1] [1,2]` and passes its 1-channel and 1-to-2 renders |
| 2 | Exactly one bypass; processing continues | the contract's one `role: bypass` is `CLAP_PARAM_IS_BYPASS`; the block keeps running, the output crossfades (10 ms) to the input delayed by the latency | `bypassKeepsProcessingAligned`: bypassed output equals the input `latency` samples late, bit for bit; released, it equals a never-bypassed plugin bit for bit; auval Bypass Effect |
| 3 | Latency set before activation, changed only via a restart request | fixed in `activate()`, reported to `clap_host_latency.changed` there if it moved; if a block's latency ever differed while active, `request_restart` | `latencyAndSampleRate`: an impulse sounds exactly the reported latency later, 200 varied calls leave it and the restart count alone, 44.1 -> 96 kHz reports the change during activation |
| 4 | Chunked state, including before activation | versioned text by contract key (`state_text.hpp`), loops over partial reads and writes, a load asks the host to rescan values | `stateBeforeActivation` (one-byte reads, three-byte writes, no activate, refuses another type, a newer version and an empty stream); clap-validator state-reproducibility (basic, binary, buffered) and invalid-state tests; pluginval state and restoration |
| 5 | Parameter flush while inactive | flush only updates the values `activate()` applies | `flushWhileInactive`; clap-validator param-set-events (flush equals process) |
| 6 | Tolerate deactivate without stop_processing | `deactivate()` clears the processing flag itself | `latencyAndSampleRate` deactivates without stopping and reactivates |
| 7 | Max block size is a bound | events cut the buffer sample-accurately, and no stretch exceeds the activated maximum | `blockSizesAndLayouts`: 1, 512, random sizes, and a 1000-frame call on a 512 maximum; clap-validator random and varying block sizes; auval Bad Max Frames |
| 8 | Read the host-information extension | `clap-wrapper.host-information/0` at `init()`: wrapper flavour and the real host's name, logged | `hostInformation` (wrapped as VST3, and plain CLAP) |
| 9 | Model/IR swap off-thread with a short crossfade | `banks.hpp`: a loader thread prepares a second bank; the audio thread takes it with one atomic exchange and crossfades 20 ms; a failed file keeps the current one and is reported through `request_callback` | `fileSwapsOffThread`: no step over 0.002 during the swap, the missing file logged, the old response kept; the audio thread's watch stays at zero while the loader allocates |
| 10 | A block's learned state and trigger parameters | `learned.hpp`: after a buffer in which a block's learned state changed, the audio thread copies it through a lock-free triple buffer; a save writes it beside the parameters (`learned N <hex>`), a load hands it back the same way. A state is refused if the block refuses its learned state; one without learned state keeps the current one. A `Role::Trigger` parameter reaches the block only as an event, never from a state load or a re-apply | cases for the blocks that learn (`tests/extra_*.cpp`): learned through the plugin, restored before activation, while active, at a new rate, in another layout, and across threads under TSan |
| - | Real-time safe `process()` | no allocation, lock or I/O; lazy symbol binding disabled (`-bind_at_load`), found by the lock watch | every `process()` call in every case is watched: 0 allocations, frees and locks; 0 RTSan reports, also over the shipped bundles; 0 TSan reports |

## Known, outside this repository

- clap-validator's `param-set-events` and `param-set-wrong-namespace` compare every parameter,
  read-only meters included, after processing audio. Meters publish at their contract rate (30 Hz)
  from one period after activation, so the validator's single 512-sample buffer never moves them,
  but a longer run would. Worth a clap-validator issue: skip `CLAP_PARAM_IS_READONLY` there.
- clap-wrapper's AUv2 `SupportsTail()` returns false although `GetTailTime()` reads `clap.tail`
  (auval: "Tail Time: Recommended Property is not supported"). A one-line upstream fix.
- Re-running CMake's configure step regenerates an AU bundle's default `Info.plist`, and
  clap-wrapper only copies its generated one when the AU relinks. `finish-bundles.cmake` restores
  it after every build and signs the bundles ad hoc.

## Real hosts

`tests/reaper-smoke.lua` runs inside REAPER: a new project tab with every installed Squatch plugin
on its own track, fed an A2 sine 13 cents sharp for 4 s with the master at -inf, then prints each
plugin's parameters as REAPER formats them (the tuner's Note should read A).

================================================================================
FILE: hosts/daisy/README.md    [Docs: squatch-dsp on the Daisy Seed3]
================================================================================

# squatch-dsp on the Daisy Seed3

Firmware that runs squatch-dsp blocks, and a Neural Amp Modeler (NAM) A2-Lite model, on an Electrosmith Daisy Seed3
(STM32H750, Cortex-M7 at 480 MHz, 128 KB internal flash). It is a measurement platform first: every image reads the
chip's cycle counter around the work it does and reports the result over USB serial, so a claim about cost is a number
read off the board.

The measured results, the method and how to repeat them are in
[docs/benchmarks/daisy-seed3.md](../../docs/benchmarks/daisy-seed3.md). Licences of what the firmware uses or was
generated
from are in [THIRD_PARTY.md](THIRD_PARTY.md).

## What you need

- `arm-none-eabi-gcc`. The numbers in the benchmark note were measured with the Arm GNU Toolchain 15.3.Rel1 (GCC
  15.3.1).
  The flash images are close to the 128 KB limit (the amp chain is 98% full), so another compiler version can overflow
  the
  link; CI pins 15.3.Rel1.
- `make`, `git`, `curl`, `python3`. `numpy` and `clang++` for the accuracy tools. `dfu-util` to flash.
- A Daisy Seed3 and a USB cable, only for flashing and measuring. Building and the host tests need no board.

## Build

```sh
hosts/daisy/fetch-libdaisy        # once: libDaisy at a pinned commit, with our two patches, into hosts/daisy/vendor/
make -C hosts/daisy -j4           # every image, their sizes (build/daisy/SIZES.md) and the heap check
```

`fetch-libdaisy` does not vendor libDaisy. It clones one commit (`facb66c7`, libDaisy master at the Seed3 DevKits merge,
2026-09-24) and the four submodules the build needs at the commits that commit records, applies the two patches in
`patches/`, and writes a stamp holding the commit and the SHA-256 of each patch. `make` re-checks the stamp and refuses
to
build if the checkout is anything else. Nothing else in the build downloads anything.

Images are named `seed3-<variant>.bin` in `build/daisy/bin/`. To build one: `make -C hosts/daisy
../../build/daisy/bin/seed3-nam-chain-b32.bin`.

## The images

A variant name is `PROJECT-OPTION-...`; `bNN` is the block size in samples (32 by default, 48 kHz).

| image | what it does |
|---|---|
| `passthrough-bNN` | AUDIO IN 1 and 2 to AUDIO OUT 1 and 2, unchanged. The first sound on a new board and the cost of doing nothing. `passthrough-crash-b32` faults on purpose after 3 s, to check that a crashed image lands in the ROM bootloader. |
| `chain-bNN` | AUDIO IN 1 through the gate, the drive and the limiter to both outputs: three squatch-dsp blocks, with the cost of each per block. Options: `hot` (a +24 dB signal), `gen` (a built-in test signal instead of the input), `laNN` (limiter look-ahead in samples), `limonly`, `burnNN` (a stage that busy-waits NN% of the budget). |
| `latency-bNN` | The Seed measures its own round trip: it writes a click to AUDIO OUT 1, you wire OUT 1 to IN 1, and it finds the click coming back. `latency-lim-...` and `latency-chain-...` put the limiter, or gate + drive + limiter, in the path. |
| `nam-b32` | The A2-Lite model alone: a built-in test input through the model to both outputs. |
| `nam-chain-b32` | Built-in input, gate, drive, A2-Lite, limiter: the whole chain on one core. This is the image the benchmark note calls the chain. |
| `nam-parity-b32` | The model alone fed fixed noise; after the model has warmed up it sends 4,800 input and output samples over serial as float bits, for `tools/nam_check.py`. |
| `nam-bench-b32-...` | Built by `tools/nam_bench.py`: runs the model from the main loop with no audio, times 150 blocks, and records the 4,800 samples. Used to compare kernel variants. |
| `notegen-b32` | A known note on AUDIO OUT 2, stepping through the open strings, with its name, exact frequency and cents printed. A signal source for testing a hardware tuner. |

`make` builds the usual set; `EXTRA_VARIANTS="name ..."` adds more. The block size, `hot`, `gen` and the other options
are
compile-time definitions (`-DSQUATCH_BLOCK=32` and so on); the Makefile's header comment lists them.

The A2-Lite images link a libDaisy built `-Os` (`vendor/libDaisy/build-os`), because at `-O2` they do not fit the
128 KB flash. The kernel itself is compiled `-O3`, which it needs (see the benchmark note).

## Flashing over DFU

Nothing is flashed by building. To put an image on a board:

1. Put the Seed3 in its ROM bootloader once: hold BOOT, tap RESET, release BOOT. It then shows up as USB `0483:df11`.
2. `SEED3_SERIAL=<serial> hosts/daisy/tools/flash.py build/daisy/bin/seed3-chain-b32.bin` writes it with
   `dfu-util -a 0 -s 0x08000000:leave -D IMAGE` and waits for the image's banner on the serial port.
   `--backup DIR` reads the old 128 KB flash into `DIR` first, with its SHA-256.

After that first press, every image here answers the line `dfu` on its USB serial port by resetting into the ROM
bootloader, so `flash.py` can reflash without touching the board. If an image crashes, a fault handler also sends it to
the
bootloader. An image whose audio callback takes longer than the block starves the main loop and cannot be told to `dfu`;
`nam-b32` and `nam-chain-b32` therefore measure one block's cost before starting audio and refuse to start it above 90%
of
the budget.

`SEED3_SERIAL` is the board's USB serial number: with only the Seed plugged in, `ls /dev/cu.usbmodem*` shows
`/dev/cu.usbmodem<serial><digit>`; give the part between. It is never guessed, because other USB boards use the same
device
names and `flash.py` writes to whatever it finds. `dfu-util` is pointed only at `0483:df11`, and it refuses to act if
more
than one such device is present. `flash.py` is written for macOS; on Linux the port is `/dev/ttyACM*` and the script
needs a
small change.

## The serial output

Each image prints one banner and then a few lines a second on the USB serial port (a USB CDC port, so any baud rate
works). The lines below are from a run of `nam-chain-b32` on an earlier tree whose limiter was cheaper (the limiter
figure differs from this tree's); they show the shape of the output, not this release's numbers.

```text
# seed3-nam-chain-b32 block=32 rate=48000 cpu=480000000Hz budget=320000 cycles/block board=seed3 libDaisy=facb66c7
# nam: A2-Lite 1871 weights, receptive field 6347, state 114048 bytes, gate drive nam limiter, latency 88 samples ready
w=5 blocks=1500 late=0 over=0 stretched=0 in=-9.0 out=-21.3 dBFS usb_ungate=1 usb_dropped=2
w=5 cpu 57.70/58.23/58.23 period 99.97/100.01/100.01 (% of block: mean/p99/worst)
w=5 gate 1.09/1.12/1.12 drive 5.92/6.25/6.28 nam 48.13/48.37/48.37 limiter 2.36/2.49/2.49
```

Before it starts audio, the nam images also print `# warm-up: N cycles/block of 320000 budget (P%) -> starting audio`.

- `w=N` is the one-second window. `blocks` is the number of audio callbacks in it (1,500 at block 32); `late` counts
  callbacks that started more than 1.5 block periods after the previous one and `over` counts callbacks whose own work
  took
  longer than a block period. Both must stay 0.
- `cpu mean/p99/worst` is the whole callback's cost as a share of the block's budget (320,000 cycles at block 32). The
  99th
  percentile comes from a 256-bin histogram, so it is exact to 1/128 of the budget; the worst is exact.
- `period` is the time between callbacks, as a share of the block. It sits at 100% when the audio clock is steady.
- one line per stage (`gate`, `drive`, `nam`, `limiter`) with the same three numbers.
- `usb_dropped` counts serial lines the board dropped because the USB buffer was full; it is a logging artefact, not
  audio.
- the latency image prints `click N: lag=81.33 samples (1.69 ms) ...` and, every 16 clicks, a `LATENCY` summary line.
- the parity image prints `DUMP begin` ... `D <start> <in:out> x 8` lines ... `DUMP end`.
- the bench image prints `# bench: block=32 mean=... min=... max=... warm=... blocks=150 budget=320000 pct=...` and
  `# stack: region=... used_hw=... never_touched=...`.

## Reproducing the benchmark

See the benchmark note's "How to reproduce" section for the whole procedure. In short:

```sh
hosts/daisy/tools/fetch-nam-model                     # NAM Core's A2.nam at a pinned commit, sha256 checked
export SEED3_SERIAL=<your board's USB serial>
hosts/daisy/tools/nam_bench.py --selftest --only 'base,fused+dtcm,fused+dtcm+slideh'
```

`nam_bench.py` builds each kernel variant, flashes it, reads the board's cycle counts and recording, scores the
recording
against a float64 reference (`tools/a2_reference.py`) fed the board's own input bits, and writes `results.csv` and
`results.md` under `build/daisy/nam-bench/`. `--selftest` adds a deliberately wrong variant that must be rejected.

## Host tests

`make test` at the repository root builds `hosts/daisy/tests/*.cpp` for the host with the sanitizers: the cycle
statistics,
the click detector, the drive block, and the A2-Lite kernel (bit-identical across block sizes, and checked against the
plain
kernel). `python3 hosts/daisy/tests/test_tools.py` tests the Python tools' guards. Neither needs a board.

## Files

| path | what |
|---|---|
| `seed3-*/main.cpp` | one firmware per project: passthrough, chain, latency, nam, notegen |
| `common/` | board support shared by the images: cycle counter, serial, window statistics, click detector |
| `nam/` | the A2-Lite kernel (`a2lite.hpp`) and the model's weights (`a2lite_weights.hpp`, generated) |
| `faust/` | the drive block and its Faust-generated core (see THIRD_PARTY.md for the licence of the generated file) |
| `tools/` | flashing, benchmark and accuracy tools, the heap check (fails an image whose audio callback can reach `malloc`), the size report |
| `patches/` | our two patches to libDaisy and why they exist (THIRD_PARTY.md) |
| `tests/` | host-side tests |

## NeuralAmpModelerCore: the model weights (MIT)

`nam/a2lite_weights.hpp` holds the 1,871 weights of the A2-Lite submodel (3 channels, 23 layers) of the example model
`example_models/A2.nam` in NeuralAmpModelerCore, <https://github.com/sdatkinson/NeuralAmpModelerCore>, commit
`0b3d3c97b0859a3a8c92a8628c4dd89a25eb5842` (sha256 of the file
`2d2d744516dc0197737a2c5001010429692d4cb20d72b08264781de626fcf4ca`).
`tools/fetch-nam-model` downloads that exact file and `tools/nam_to_header.py` regenerates the header from it. The
network
layout in `nam/a2lite.hpp` follows NAM Core's A2 WaveNet; the code is our own. Nothing trained on any other capture is
here.

## libDaisy (MIT), fetched, not copied

The firmware links Electrosmith's libDaisy, <https://github.com/electro-smith/libDaisy>. It is not vendored:
`fetch-libdaisy`
clones commit `facb66c76b5482918741695f4268b0185e474644` (master at the Seed3 DevKits merge, 2026-09-24; no tagged
release has
Seed3 support) and its four submodules at the commits that commit records, into `vendor/` (gitignored), and refuses to
build
if anything differs. The libDaisy licence travels with the checkout (`vendor/libDaisy/LICENSE`); its notice is:

```text
The MIT License (MIT)

Copyright (c) 2019 Electrosmith

Permission is hereby granted, free of charge, to any person obtaining a copy
of this software and associated documentation files (the "Software"), to deal
in the Software without restriction, including without limitation the rights
to use, copy, modify, merge, publish, distribute, sublicense, and/or sell
copies of the Software, and to permit persons to whom the Software is
furnished to do so, subject to the following conditions:

The above copyright notice and this permission notice shall be included in
all copies or substantial portions of the Software.

THE SOFTWARE IS PROVIDED "AS IS", WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND, EXPRESS OR
IMPLIED, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO THE WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY,
FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE AND NONINFRINGEMENT. IN NO EVENT SHALL THE
AUTHORS OR COPYRIGHT HOLDERS BE LIABLE FOR ANY CLAIM, DAMAGES OR OTHER
LIABILITY, WHETHER IN AN ACTION OF CONTRACT, TORT OR OTHERWISE, ARISING FROM,
OUT OF OR IN CONNECTION WITH THE SOFTWARE OR THE USE OR OTHER DEALINGS IN THE
SOFTWARE.
```

libDaisy's own submodules (ARM CMSIS, STMicroelectronics' CMSIS device files, HAL driver and USB device library) carry
their own licences inside the fetched checkout; none of their files is copied into this repository. A firmware binary
you
build contains parts of them, so keep those licence files with any binary you distribute.

### Our two patches to libDaisy, and why each exists

Both are applied by `fetch-libdaisy` from `patches/`, and both come from upstream pull requests (kept here because
libDaisy
has not released a version with them). Neither changes the Make build this folder uses; they matter to anyone who builds
libDaisy with CMake.

| patch | what | why |
|---|---|---|
| `0001-cmake-define-DATA_IN_D2_SRAM.patch` | libDaisy PR #713 (fixes #712) | The CMake build never defined `DATA_IN_D2_SRAM`, so `SystemInit()` left the D2 SRAM, which holds the audio DMA buffers, switched off. The Make build already defines it. |
| `0002-linker-scripts-drop-malformed-DISCARD.patch` | libDaisy PR #715 (fixes #714) | A malformed `DISCARD` block in the linker scripts named `libc.a`, `libm.a` and `libgcc.a`, which made CMake links load all of newlib. The Make link is byte-identical with or without it. |

## Faust libraries: the generated drive (`faust/drive_faust.hpp`)

`faust/drive_faust.hpp` is the C++ output of the Faust compiler 2.85.9 for an overdrive model that is our own work,
adapted by
`faust/generate`. The licence lines of the Faust libraries it was compiled from were read in that release's
`share/faust`
on 2026-10-17:

| library and functions used | licence line in the file | effect on this header |
|---|---|---|
| `filters.lib`: `highpass`, `lowpass`, `tf1`, `tf1s` | "Copyright (C) 2003-2019 by Julius O. Smith III", "MIT-style STK-4.3 license" | permissive; the copyright and permission notice must stay with copies: it is printed below and in the header of `drive_faust.hpp` |
| `signals.lib`, "jos section": `smooth` (`smoo`) | "Copyright (C) 2003-2017 by Julius O. Smith III ... released under the (MIT-style) STK-4.3 license" | same |
| `maths.lib` (`tanh`, `PI`), `platform.lib` (`SR`), `signals.lib` GRAME section | "Copyright (C) 2003-2016 / 2020 GRAME", "GNU Lesser General Public License ... EXCEPTION TO THE LGPL LICENSE" | the exception lets you "freely choose the license for the resulting compiled code ... no obligation to be LGPL or GPL", so MIT is allowed |

The Faust compiler itself (LGPL 2.1 or later) is not part of this repository, and no Faust architecture file is
included: the
header is the bare generated class, with the Faust UI and metadata members removed.

```text
STK 4.3 licence (Julius O. Smith III), as printed at the end of Faust's filters.lib:

Permission is hereby granted, free of charge, to any person obtaining a copy of
this software and associated documentation files (the "Software"), to deal in
the Software without restriction, including without limitation the rights to
use, copy, modify, merge, publish, distribute, sublicense, and/or sell copies
of the Software, and to permit persons to whom the Software is furnished to do
so, subject to the following conditions:

The above copyright notice and this permission notice shall be included in all
copies or substantial portions of the Software.

Any person wishing to distribute modifications to the Software is asked to send
the modifications to the original developer so that they can be incorporated
into the canonical version.  For software copyrighted by Julius O. Smith III,
email your modifications to him at the address printed in Faust's filters.lib.  This is, however, not a
binding provision of this license.

THE SOFTWARE IS PROVIDED "AS IS", WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND, EXPRESS OR
IMPLIED, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO THE WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY,
FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE AND NONINFRINGEMENT.  IN NO EVENT SHALL THE
AUTHORS OR COPYRIGHT HOLDERS BE LIABLE FOR ANY CLAIM, DAMAGES OR OTHER
```

The Faust source of the model is not published, so `faust/generate` cannot be run from this repository (it stays as the
record of exactly how the header was made). The firmware builds from the committed header.

```yaml
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# Every push and pull request: the standalone header check, the library and the sanitizer tests
# pass; on pushes (main), published files match EXPORTED. Complexity is in quality.yml.
name: CI
on:
  push:
  pull_request:
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Published files match EXPORTED (enforced on main)
        if: github.event_name == 'push'
        run: python3 tools/export-public dsp --verify .
      - name: Published files this pull request edits (applied upstream on merge)
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        run: python3 tools/export-public dsp --verify . || true
      - name: Headers, library and tests (ASan + UBSan, TSan)
        run: |
          # ThreadSanitizer cannot map its shadow memory with the kernel's default 32 bits of
          # mmap randomisation on this image.
          sudo sysctl -w vm.mmap_rnd_bits=28
          make headers lib test CXX=clang++
```

================================================================================
FILE: .github/workflows/daisy.yml    [Build and run: .github/workflows/daisy.yml]
================================================================================

```yaml
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# The Daisy Seed3 firmware: every image builds with a pinned arm-none-eabi-gcc, fits the 128 KB flash, passes the heap check,
# and the host-side tests pass. Nothing is flashed: no board is involved.
name: Daisy
on:
  push:
  pull_request:
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  firmware:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    env:
      # Arm GNU Toolchain 15.3.Rel1 (GCC 15.3.1), the compiler the benchmark in docs/benchmarks/daisy-seed3.md was measured with.
      # The chain image is 98% of the flash, so another compiler may not link. Published by Arm at gitlab.arm.com (its .sha256asc
      # file carries the same digest); GCC 15.3.1 is dated 2026-06-27.
      ARM_GCC_VERSION: 15.3.rel1
      ARM_GCC_SHA256: 563bebb2b97d53382b956d6ee1fe61e2cae26699901417234a37df505ef9b5fa
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: arm-none-eabi-gcc ${{ env.ARM_GCC_VERSION }} (pinned by hash)
        run: |
          name="arm-gnu-toolchain-${ARM_GCC_VERSION}-x86_64-arm-none-eabi"
          curl --fail --silent --show-error --location --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/gcc.tar.xz" \
            "https://gitlab.arm.com/api/v4/projects/tooling%2Fgnu-toolchains-for-arm/packages/generic/gnu-toolchain/${ARM_GCC_VERSION}/${name}.tar.xz"
          echo "${ARM_GCC_SHA256}  $RUNNER_TEMP/gcc.tar.xz" | sha256sum --check --strict
          tar -xJf "$RUNNER_TEMP/gcc.tar.xz" -C "$RUNNER_TEMP"
          echo "$RUNNER_TEMP/$name/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
      - name: Toolchain version
        run: arm-none-eabi-gcc --version | head -1
      - name: libDaisy at the pinned commit, with our two patches
        run: hosts/daisy/fetch-libdaisy
      - name: Build every image, check sizes and the heap
        run: make -C hosts/daisy -j4
      - name: Image sizes
        run: cat build/daisy/SIZES.md >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
      - name: The model weights header regenerates from NAM Core's example model
        run: |
          hosts/daisy/tools/fetch-nam-model
          python3 hosts/daisy/tools/nam_to_header.py build/nam-model/A2.nam | diff - hosts/daisy/nam/a2lite_weights.hpp
      - name: Host-side tests (ASan + UBSan, allocation watch)
        run: |
          sudo sysctl -w vm.mmap_rnd_bits=28
          make build/test_daisy CXX=clang++
          ./build/test_daisy
      - name: Tool guard tests (the accuracy-gate test needs numpy)
        run: |
          sudo apt-get install --yes --no-install-recommends python3-numpy
          python3 hosts/daisy/tests/test_tools.py
```
